question_text: Which of the following is a colligative property?

options.label: A
options.text: Boiling point

options.label: B
options.text: Freezing point

options.label: C
options.text: Osmotic pressure

options.label: D
options.text: Surface tension

explanation: Colligative properties are properties of solutions that depend on the ratio of the number of solute particles to the number of solvent particles in a solution, and not on the nature of the chemical species present. Osmotic pressure is one such property.

question_text: What is the IUPAC name of the complex [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2?

options.label: A
options.text: Pentamminechloridocobalt(II) chloride

options.label: B
options.text: Pentamminechloridocobalt(III) chloride

options.label: C
options.text: Pentamminechlorocobalt(II) chloride

options.label: D
options.text: Pentamminechlorocobalt(III) chloride

explanation: The oxidation state of Co is +3. The ligands are five ammine (NH3) and one chloro (Cl). The IUPAC name is Pentamminechlorocobalt(III) chloride.

question_text: Which of the following compounds will give a positive iodoform test?

options.label: A
options.text: Ethanol

options.label: B
options.text: Methanol

options.label: C
options.text: Propanal

options.label: D
options.text: Benzaldehyde

explanation: Iodoform test is given by compounds containing the CH3CO- group or CH3CH(OH)- group. Ethanol (CH3CH2OH) contains the CH3CH(OH)- group and will give a positive iodoform test.

question_text: What is the effect of Schottky defect on the density of the crystal?

options.label: A
options.text: Increases

options.label: B
options.text: Decreases

options.label: C
options.text: Remains the same

options.label: D
options.text: Cannot be predicted

explanation: Schottky defect involves missing of ions from the lattice site. Thus, the mass decreases while the volume remains the same, hence the density decreases.

question_text: Write the IUPAC name of the following compound: CH3CH(CH3)CH2CHO

options.label: A
options.text: 2-methylbutanal

options.label: B
options.text: 3-methylbutanal

options.label: C
options.text: 2-methylpentanal

options.label: D
options.text: 3-methylpentanal

explanation: The longest carbon chain containing the aldehyde group has 4 carbons. The methyl group is at the 3rd position. Hence, the IUPAC name is 3-methylbutanal.

question_text: Define the term 'rate constant' of a reaction.

options.label: A
options.text: The rate of reaction when the concentration of each reactant is unity.

options.label: B
options.text: The rate of reaction when the concentration of each reactant is zero.

options.label: C
options.text: The rate of reaction at equilibrium.

options.label: D
options.text: The rate of reaction at standard temperature and pressure.

explanation: The rate constant (k) is the proportionality constant in the rate law expression. It is equal to the rate of the reaction when the concentration of each reactant is unity.

question_text: What are lyophilic colloids? Give one example.

options.label: A
options.text: Colloids that are water-hating; Gold sol

options.label: B
options.text: Colloids that are solvent-loving; Starch sol

options.label: C
options.text: Colloids that are easily coagulated; Fe(OH)3 sol

options.label: D
options.text: Colloids that are formed by physical methods; As2S3 sol

explanation: Lyophilic colloids are solvent-loving colloids. They are directly formed by mixing with the solvent. Example: Starch sol.

question_text: Write the mechanism of hydration of ethene to yield ethanol.

options.label: A
options.text: Electrophilic addition followed by nucleophilic attack

options.label: B
options.text: Nucleophilic addition followed by electrophilic attack

options.label: C
options.text: Electrophilic addition followed by protonation

options.label: D
options.text: Electrophilic addition followed by deprotonation

explanation: The mechanism involves protonation of ethene to form carbocation, followed by nucleophilic attack of water and finally deprotonation to form ethanol.

question_text: Explain the following terms: (i) Inversion of sugar (ii) Mutarotation

options.label: A
options.text: Both involve change in optical rotation; Inversion is specific to sucrose

options.label: B
options.text: Both involve change in optical rotation; Mutarotation is specific to sucrose

options.label: C
options.text: Inversion involves hydrolysis; Mutarotation involves change in pH

options.label: D
options.text: Inversion involves change in pH; Mutarotation involves hydrolysis

explanation: Inversion of sugar refers to the change in sign of optical rotation from dextro (+) to levo (-) upon hydrolysis of sucrose. Mutarotation is the change in optical rotation because of the change in the equilibrium between two anomers, when the corresponding stereocenters interconvert.

question_text: Describe the preparation of potassium permanganate from pyrolusite ore.

options.label: A
options.text: Reduction of MnO2 with KOH, followed by oxidation

options.label: B
options.text: Oxidation of MnO2 with KOH, followed by electrolysis

options.label: C
options.text: Oxidation of MnO2 with KOH, followed by acidification

options.label: D
options.text: Oxidation of MnO2 with KOH, followed by oxidation

explanation: Pyrolusite ore (MnO2) is fused with KOH in the presence of air or an oxidizing agent like KNO3 to form potassium manganate (K2MnO4). This manganate is then electrolytically or by oxidation converted to potassium permanganate (KMnO4).

question_text: Account for the following: (i) Transition metals form complex compounds. (ii) Zn, Cd and Hg are not regarded as transition elements.

options.label: A
options.text: Variable oxidation states, incomplete d-orbitals; Complete d-orbitals

options.label: B
options.text: Fixed oxidation states, incomplete d-orbitals; Incomplete d-orbitals

options.label: C
options.text: Variable oxidation states, complete d-orbitals; Complete d-orbitals

options.label: D
options.text: Fixed oxidation states, complete d-orbitals; Incomplete d-orbitals

explanation: Transition metals form complexes due to small size, high charge, availability of vacant d-orbitals and variable oxidation states. Zn, Cd, and Hg have completely filled d-orbitals in their ground state and common oxidation states, hence not considered transition elements.

question_text: Write the Nernst equation for the cell reaction: Zn(s) + Cu2+(aq) → Zn2+(aq) + Cu(s)

options.label: A
options.text: Ecell = E°cell - (0.0591/2) log([Zn2+]/[Cu2+])

options.label: B
options.text: Ecell = E°cell + (0.0591/2) log([Zn2+]/[Cu2+])

options.label: C
options.text: Ecell = E°cell - (0.0591/1) log([Zn2+]/[Cu2+])

options.label: D
options.text: Ecell = E°cell + (0.0591/1) log([Zn2+]/[Cu2+])

explanation: The Nernst equation for the given cell reaction is Ecell = E°cell - (RT/nF) ln([Zn2+]/[Cu2+]). At 298K, this simplifies to Ecell = E°cell - (0.0591/2) log([Zn2+]/[Cu2+]), where n=2 is the number of electrons transferred.

question_text: What is meant by 'rate of a reaction'? What are the factors that affect the rate of a reaction?

options.label: A
options.text: Change in concentration per unit time; Temperature, pressure, catalyst

options.label: B
options.text: Change in concentration per unit time; Temperature, concentration, catalyst

options.label: C
options.text: Change in volume per unit time; Temperature, concentration, catalyst

options.label: D
options.text: Change in volume per unit time; Temperature, pressure, catalyst

explanation: Rate of reaction is the change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time. Factors affecting the rate include temperature, concentration of reactants, catalyst, and surface area.

question_text: Differentiate between physisorption and chemisorption.

options.label: A
options.text: Weak forces, reversible; Strong forces, irreversible

options.label: B
options.text: Strong forces, reversible; Weak forces, irreversible

options.label: C
options.text: High enthalpy, reversible; Low enthalpy, irreversible

options.label: D
options.text: High enthalpy, irreversible; Low enthalpy, reversible

explanation: Physisorption involves weak van der Waals forces, is reversible, and has low enthalpy of adsorption. Chemisorption involves strong chemical bonds, is irreversible, and has high enthalpy of adsorption.

question_text: Write the structures of the monomers of the following polymers: (i) Buna-S (ii) Nylon-6

options.label: A
options.text: Styrene, Caprolactam

options.label: B
options.text: Butadiene, Caprolactam

options.label: C
options.text: Styrene and Butadiene, Caprolactam

options.label: D
options.text: Styrene and Butadiene, Adipic acid

explanation: Buna-S is a copolymer of styrene and butadiene. Nylon-6 is a polymer of caprolactam.

question_text: What are antiseptic and disinfectant? Give one example of each.

options.label: A
options.text: Applied to living tissues, applied to inanimate objects; Phenol, Dettol

options.label: B
options.text: Applied to living tissues, applied to inanimate objects; Dettol, Phenol

options.label: C
options.text: Applied to inanimate objects, applied to living tissues; Phenol, Dettol

options.label: D
options.text: Applied to inanimate objects, applied to living tissues; Dettol, Phenol

explanation: Antiseptics are applied to living tissues to inhibit the growth of microorganisms (e.g., Dettol). Disinfectants are applied to inanimate objects (e.g., Phenol).

question_text: Explain the following reactions: (i) Wolff-Kishner Reduction (ii) Cannizzaro Reaction

options.label: A
options.text: Reduction to alkane, disproportionation of aldehydes

options.label: B
options.text: Oxidation to alcohol, reduction to alkane

options.label: C
options.text: Reduction to alcohol, oxidation to acid

options.label: D
options.text: Oxidation to acid, reduction to alcohol

explanation: Wolff-Kishner reduction converts carbonyl group to CH2 group using hydrazine and strong base. Cannizzaro reaction is a disproportionation reaction of aldehydes lacking α-hydrogen in the presence of a strong base.

question_text: How do you convert: (i) Phenol to Anisole (ii) Ethanol to Propan-2-ol

options.label: A
options.text: Williamson synthesis, Hydration

options.label: B
options.text: Williamson synthesis, Dehydration followed by hydration

options.label: C
options.text: Wurtz reaction, Hydration

options.label: D
options.text: Wurtz reaction, Dehydration followed by hydration

explanation: Phenol to Anisole involves Williamson ether synthesis (reacting sodium phenoxide with methyl halide). Ethanol to Propan-2-ol involves dehydration to ethene followed by hydration to propan-2-ol.

question_text: Give reasons for the following: (i) Haloarenes are less reactive than haloalkanes towards nucleophilic substitution reactions. (ii) Although chlorine is an electron withdrawing group, yet it is ortho-para directing in electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions.

options.label: A
options.text: Resonance stabilization, Resonance effect

options.label: B
options.text: Inductive effect, Resonance effect

options.label: C
options.text: Resonance stabilization, Inductive effect

options.label: D
options.text: Inductive effect, Inductive effect

explanation: Haloarenes are less reactive due to resonance stabilization. Chlorine is ortho-para directing due to resonance effect, which increases electron density at ortho and para positions.

question_text: Define the following terms: (i) Order of a reaction (ii) Activation energy

options.label: A
options.text: Sum of powers of conc., energy required for reaction

options.label: B
options.text: Sum of powers of conc., minimum energy for reaction

options.label: C
options.text: Number of molecules reacting, energy required for reaction

options.label: D
options.text: Number of molecules reacting, minimum energy for reaction

explanation: Order of a reaction is the sum of the powers of the concentration terms in the rate law expression. Activation energy is the minimum energy required for a reaction to occur.

topic: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements

question_text: Give reasons for the following: (i) NH3 is more basic than PH3. (ii) H2S is more acidic than H2O.

options.label: A
options.text: Smaller size, larger size

options.label: B
options.text: Higher electronegativity, lower bond dissociation enthalpy

options.label: C
options.text: Smaller size, higher bond dissociation enthalpy

options.label: D
options.text: Higher electronegativity, larger size

explanation: NH3 is more basic due to higher electronegativity of N and smaller size, leading to higher electron density. H2S is more acidic due to lower bond dissociation enthalpy of H-S bond compared to H-O bond.

question_text: a) Account for the following: (i) Although F is more electronegative than Cl, HF has a lower dissociation enthalpy than HCl. (ii) Dioxygen is a gas while Sulphur is a solid. (iii) R3P=O exists but R3N=O does not (where R = alkyl group).

options.label: A
options.text: H-bonding, intermolecular forces, d-orbital availability

options.label: B
options.text: Van der Waals forces, intermolecular forces, d-orbital availability

options.label: C
options.text: H-bonding, catenation, d-orbital availability

options.label: D
options.text: Van der Waals forces, catenation, d-orbital availability

explanation: HF has lower dissociation enthalpy due to strong H-bonding. Dioxygen is a gas due to weak intermolecular forces, while Sulphur is a solid due to catenation and stronger intermolecular forces. R3P=O exists due to availability of d-orbitals in P, allowing multiple bonding, while N lacks d-orbitals.
